arguments.subject: First-Year Retention Planning committee summary
arguments.body:
First-Year Retention Planning
Wed Apr 29, 2026, Room: Cedar (Zoom)
Minutes of the official discussion through Dr. Hannah Lee's 10:58 wrap.

Attendees: Dr. Hannah Lee (host, Chair, Student Success Committee), Daniel Okafor (Senior Academic Adviser), Rosa Martinez (First-Year Success Program Coordinator).

Agenda: early-alert platform shortlist, pilot sizing, fall budget, outreach timeline.

Platform shortlist. Rosa Martinez compared EAB Navigate, Starfish, and Civitas Learning.
- Navigate has the strongest integration with Banner. About 92% of the data fields, including midterm grades, holds, and registration status, sync natively. It runs about $14.50 per student per year.
- Starfish is at $13.20 per student, and Banner coverage is more like 78%. Its adviser-workflow ratings are slightly higher.
- Civitas is the cheapest at $10.80 per student, but Banner coverage is only around 60%. It leans heavily on predictive analytics without much adviser workflow.
Decision: Navigate and Starfish move to a deeper RFP, and Civitas is out.
Rosa Martinez will draft the RFP doc this week, have it in the shared drive by end of day Friday, and share it for review by Monday.

Pilot. Decision: a 120-student pilot drawn from College of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences first-years, with a 4-week opt-in window.
Daniel Okafor will own the intake outreach.

Fall budget. Gregory confirmed the $185k envelope.
- $30k for platform demos and onboarding
- $20k for outreach comms: videos, the portal page, and an adviser toolkit
- The remaining $135k is the program spend
The $20k comms number assumes no outside production firm for the launch video.
Daniel Okafor will reflect that in the budget tracker today.
Dr. Hannah Lee will update Gregory on the platform decision and the timeline.

Outreach timeline. Decision: an Aug 10 briefing for faculty and advisers, with a full briefing pack, FAQ, and talking points, followed by an Aug 24 student-facing launch.
Rosa Martinez will own the briefing pack.
Daniel Okafor will own the student-facing launch comms in coordination with Keiko on the admissions side.

Check-in: weekly for the next three weeks, same time next Wednesday, with this slot held through the end of the semester.

Program scope. Phase 1 is the early-alert and proactive-advising outreach piece. Phase 2 is the peer-mentoring and study-skills curriculum, spring at the earliest. Phase 1 only for the pilot.

Metrics: alert-response rate, a satisfaction survey from pilot students, fall-to-spring persistence, and a faculty-experience survey at day 60. The three questions are: did you raise an alert, did you feel equipped to talk with the student about it, and did you refer anyone to advising.
Rosa Martinez will add those to the program brief.

10:58 wrap. Dr. Hannah Lee: "Okay, I think that's everything on my list. Let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused."


11:03–11:08 discussion, copied from the transcript:
[11:03 AM] Daniel Okafor: Speaking of students falling through the cracks, all this retention talk has me thinking about Jordan Ellis. You know Jordan, the sophomore I picked up from you in the fall? Jordan's term GPA came in at a 1.6.
[11:04 AM] Daniel Okafor: Failed both gateway courses, Calc II and Intro Chem. That's what puts Jordan below the line for academic probation this term.
[11:04 AM] Rosa Martinez: Oof. That's rough. Wasn't Jordan on an accommodation plan with disability services?
[11:05 AM] Daniel Okafor: Was. The accommodation letter lapsed at the start of the term and never got renewed, so no extended testing time on any of the exams. And this is on top of the medical withdrawal Jordan took last spring.
[11:05 AM] Rosa Martinez: Oh no. I remember that withdrawal. It was a hard semester. And the probation appeal is due Friday, right? Has Jordan even started it?
[11:06 AM] Daniel Okafor: Barely. Honestly, between us, I think I'm going to ask Gregory for an exception on the appeal deadline, at least until the accommodation letter is sorted. Let's keep this between the two of us for now. And I might push back on Hannah about the outreach sequencing. Waiting until Aug 24 is too late for students like Jordan.
[11:06 AM] Rosa Martinez: I've been thinking the same. And the appeal should reference the lapsed letter. The failed exams happened without the testing accommodations Jordan was entitled to.
[11:06 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yeah. Jordan's basically the exact student this whole initiative is supposed to catch, huh.
[11:07 AM] Rosa Martinez: Right? And if the appeal doesn't go through, Jordan loses the scholarship too. That's the part that worries me most.
[11:07 AM] Daniel Okafor: Agreed. Want to grab coffee later this week and go through Jordan's file properly before I reach out?
[11:07 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yes please. Thursday afternoon?
[11:08 AM] Daniel Okafor: Thursday works. I'll text you.
[11:08 AM] Rosa Martinez: Anyway, I should head out. See you Friday.
[11:08 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yeah, take care.

Morning. Yep, ready.
Hey Hannah, hey Daniel. Ready.

Great. Agenda: early-alert platform shortlist, pilot sizing, fall budget, outreach timeline. Let's start with the platform shortlist. Rosa, you took the deeper look at the three platforms. Which ones are we recommending we advance?

So I went through EAB Navigate, Starfish, and Civitas Learning. Quick read: Navigate has the strongest integration with our Banner student information system. About 92% of the data fields we'd want, including midterm grades, holds, and registration status, sync natively. It runs about $14.50 per student per year at our enrollment tier. Starfish is at $13.20 per student, and Banner coverage is more like 78%, but its adviser-workflow ratings are slightly higher in the third-party reviews I pulled. Civitas is the cheapest at $10.80 per student, but Banner coverage for us is only around 60%. It also leans heavily on predictive analytics without much adviser workflow, which I don't think fits what we're trying to build.
Yeah, I'd drop Civitas. A risk score is fine for some schools, but our advisers are going to need an actual case-management workflow on the other end.
Agreed. So we advance Navigate and Starfish to a deeper RFP and drop Civitas?
Yes, that's my recommendation.
Plus one.
Good. Decision: Navigate and Starfish move to RFP, and Civitas is out. Rosa, can you draft the RFP doc this week and share it for review by Monday?
Will do. I'll have it in the shared drive by end of day Friday.
Perfect. Item two, pilot cohort. I want to land on a number today. Daniel, what's your read?

I've been going back and forth. With anything under 100 students we won't have enough signal to evaluate. With anything over 200 we're basically launching, not piloting. I'd land at 120. That's big enough to see real alert-and-response patterns, and small enough that if something is off with the platform we can pull the plug without it being campus-wide.

I'd second 120. On cohort selection, I'd suggest we pull from College of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences first-years. Two reasons. Those are our two highest DFW-rate populations per the institutional research report, so the signal will be clearest there. They're also both sized so that 120 students splits cleanly without forcing us to mix three colleges.
That works for me. Any concern about selection bias if we only pull from those two colleges?
Some, but I think the trade-off is worth it for the pilot. We can broaden in the full launch.

Okay. Decision: a 120-student pilot drawn from College of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences first-years, with a 4-week opt-in window so students can sign up on their own schedule. Daniel, you'll own the intake outreach?
Yep.
Good. Item three, fall budget. Gregory confirmed the $185k envelope last week. Rosa, how do we want to slice it?

I'd carve out $30k for platform demos and onboarding and $20k for outreach comms: videos, the portal page, and an adviser toolkit. The remaining $135k would be the actual program spend. With 120 pilot students plus peer-mentor stipends and tutoring hours, that gets us comfortably through fall and spring with margin for the full launch ramp.
That math works. I'd just flag that the $20k comms number assumes we don't end up needing an outside production firm for the launch video. If we do, that goes up.

Noted. We can revisit if university marketing can't turn it around. Decision: the fall envelope is $185k, with $30k for platform demos and onboarding, $20k for outreach comms, and $135k for program. Daniel, please reflect that in the budget tracker today.
On it.

Last item, outreach timeline. I want to be thoughtful here. If we announce too early, we create anxiety about who's in the pilot and who isn't. If we announce too late, faculty and advisers feel blindsided. Where do we land?

My proposal is an Aug 10 briefing for faculty and advisers, with a full briefing pack, FAQ, and talking points, followed by an Aug 24 student-facing launch. That gives faculty and advisers two weeks to be the trusted first source if students ask questions.
I like that. The two-week adviser-first window worked well for us on the last two advising rollouts.
Agreed. Decision: Aug 10 faculty and adviser briefing, Aug 24 student-facing launch. Rosa, you'll own the briefing pack?
Yes.
And Daniel, you'll own the student-facing launch comms in coordination with Keiko on the admissions side, since some of this overlaps with the admitted-student yield messaging?
Yep, I'll loop Keiko in this week.

Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items. Rosa: RFP draft by Friday, and owner of the briefing pack. Daniel: pilot intake outreach, budget tracker update today, and student-facing launch comms with Keiko. Me: I'll update Gregory on the platform decision and the timeline. Anything I'm missing?
I think that covers it.
One thing: do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and Aug 10? I'd suggest weekly for the next three weeks given how much we have to land.
Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through the end of the semester.
Works.
Works.

One more thing while I have you both. On the program scope itself, are we still aligned that Phase 1 is the early-alert and proactive-advising outreach piece, and Phase 2 is the peer-mentoring and study-skills curriculum? I don't want us to scope-creep into Phase 2 during the pilot.
Aligned. Phase 1 only for the pilot. The peer-mentoring curriculum is spring at the earliest.
Same.
Great. On metrics, I have alert-response rate, a satisfaction survey from pilot students, and fall-to-spring persistence from the platform's reporting. Anything else you want to track?
I'd add a faculty-experience survey at day 60. Just three questions: did you raise an alert, did you feel equipped to talk with the student about it, and did you refer anyone to advising.
Plus one on that. Cheap signal, useful.
Added. So the metrics are alert-response rate, student satisfaction, fall-to-spring persistence, and the day-60 faculty survey. Rosa, please add those to the program brief.
Will do.
Okay, anything else from either of you before I let you go?
Nothing from me.
Nothing here.
Okay, I think that's everything on my list. Let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused.
Thanks Hannah, good session.
Yeah, productive. Talk soon!
Alright, I've got to jump to my 11. Talk soon.
Did you see facilities took over Cedar for the rest of the week? I had my Thursday advisee block booked in there.
Yeah, they posted it this morning. Something about the HVAC. I shifted mine to Birch.

I'll be there. Last time it ran long, so I blocked the hour after just in case.

Same thing happened to me. I asked IT to walk me through it. The old appointment codes don't carry over.
And the coffee machine on three is out again. I stood there a full minute before I noticed the tag.
That's the second time this month. I've started bringing a thermos.
Anyway. That college restructure note from last month is still sitting in my inbox. I keep meaning to open the org chart they attached.
I skimmed it. A couple of departments moved under Arts & Sciences. A lot of names to keep straight.

Speaking of students falling through the cracks, all this retention talk has me thinking about Jordan Ellis. You know Jordan, the sophomore I picked up from you in the fall? Jordan's term GPA came in at a 1.6.
Failed both gateway courses, Calc II and Intro Chem. That's what puts Jordan below the line for academic probation this term.

Thursday works. I'll text you.
Anyway, I should head out. See you Friday.

[10:34 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yeah, I'd drop Civitas. A risk score is fine for some schools, but our advisers are going to need an actual case-management workflow on the other end.
[10:34 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Agreed. So we advance Navigate and Starfish to a deeper RFP and drop Civitas?
[10:35 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yes, that's my recommendation.
[10:35 AM] Daniel Okafor: Plus one.
[10:35 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Good. Decision: Navigate and Starfish move to RFP, and Civitas is out. Rosa, can you draft the RFP doc this week and share it for review by Monday?
[10:36 AM] Rosa Martinez: Will do. I'll have it in the shared drive by end of day Friday.
[10:36 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Perfect. Item two, pilot cohort. I want to land on a number today. Daniel, what's your read?
[10:37 AM] Daniel Okafor: I've been going back and forth. With anything under 100 students we won't have enough signal to evaluate. With anything over 200 we're basically launching, not piloting. I'd land at 120. That's big enough to see real alert-and-response patterns, and small enough that if something is off with the platform we can pull the plug without it being campus-wide.
[10:38 AM] Rosa Martinez: I'd second 120. On cohort selection, I'd suggest we pull from College of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences first-years. Two reasons. Those are our two highest DFW-rate populations per the institutional research report, so the signal will be clearest there. They're also both sized so that 120 students splits cleanly without forcing us to mix three colleges.
[10:39 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: That works for me. Any concern about selection bias if we only pull from those two colleges?
[10:39 AM] Daniel Okafor: Some, but I think the trade-off is worth it for the pilot. We can broaden in the full launch.
[10:40 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Okay. Decision: a 120-student pilot drawn from College of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences first-years, with a 4-week opt-in window so students can sign up on their own schedule. Daniel, you'll own the intake outreach?
[10:40 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yep.
[10:41 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Good. Item three, fall budget. Gregory confirmed the $185k envelope last week. Rosa, how do we want to slice it?
[10:41 AM] Rosa Martinez: I'd carve out $30k for platform demos and onboarding and $20k for outreach comms: videos, the portal page, and an adviser toolkit. The remaining $135k would be the actual program spend. With 120 pilot students plus peer-mentor stipends and tutoring hours, that gets us comfortably through fall and spring with margin for the full launch ramp.
[10:43 AM] Daniel Okafor: That math works. I'd just flag that the $20k comms number assumes we don't end up needing an outside production firm for the launch video. If we do, that goes up.
[10:43 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Noted. We can revisit if university marketing can't turn it around. Decision: the fall envelope is $185k, with $30k for platform demos and onboarding, $20k for outreach comms, and $135k for program. Daniel, please reflect that in the budget tracker today.
[10:44 AM] Daniel Okafor: On it.
[10:44 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Last item, outreach timeline. I want to be thoughtful here. If we announce too early, we create anxiety about who's in the pilot and who isn't. If we announce too late, faculty and advisers feel blindsided. Where do we land?
[10:45 AM] Rosa Martinez: My proposal is an Aug 10 briefing for faculty and advisers, with a full briefing pack, FAQ, and talking points, followed by an Aug 24 student-facing launch. That gives faculty and advisers two weeks to be the trusted first source if students ask questions.
[10:46 AM] Daniel Okafor: I like that. The two-week adviser-first window worked well for us on the last two advising rollouts.
[10:46 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Agreed. Decision: Aug 10 faculty and adviser briefing, Aug 24 student-facing launch. Rosa, you'll own the briefing pack?
[10:47 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yes.
[10:47 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: And Daniel, you'll own the student-facing launch comms in coordination with Keiko on the admissions side, since some of this overlaps with the admitted-student yield messaging?
[10:48 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yep, I'll loop Keiko in this week.
[10:48 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items. Rosa: RFP draft by Friday, and owner of the briefing pack. Daniel: pilot intake outreach, budget tracker update today, and student-facing launch comms with Keiko. Me: I'll update Gregory on the platform decision and the timeline. Anything I'm missing?
[10:50 AM] Rosa Martinez: I think that covers it.
[10:50 AM] Daniel Okafor: One thing: do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and Aug 10? I'd suggest weekly for the next three weeks given how much we have to land.
[10:51 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through the end of the semester.
[10:51 AM] Daniel Okafor: Works.
[10:51 AM] Rosa Martinez: Works.
[10:52 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: One more thing while I have you both. On the program scope itself, are we still aligned that Phase 1 is the early-alert and proactive-advising outreach piece, and Phase 2 is the peer-mentoring and study-skills curriculum? I don't want us to scope-creep into Phase 2 during the pilot.
[10:53 AM] Rosa Martinez: Aligned. Phase 1 only for the pilot. The peer-mentoring curriculum is spring at the earliest.
[10:53 AM] Daniel Okafor: Same.
[10:54 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Great. On metrics, I have alert-response rate, a satisfaction survey from pilot students, and fall-to-spring persistence from the platform's reporting. Anything else you want to track?
[10:55 AM] Rosa Martinez: I'd add a faculty-experience survey at day 60. Just three questions: did you raise an alert, did you feel equipped to talk with the student about it, and did you refer anyone to advising.
[10:55 AM] Daniel Okafor: Plus one on that. Cheap signal, useful.
[10:56 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Added. So the metrics are alert-response rate, student satisfaction, fall-to-spring persistence, and the day-60 faculty survey. Rosa, please add those to the program brief.
[10:56 AM] Rosa Martinez: Will do.
[10:57 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Okay, anything else from either of you before I let you go?
[10:57 AM] Daniel Okafor: Nothing from me.
[10:57 AM] Rosa Martinez: Nothing here.
[10:58 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Okay, I think that's everything on my list. Let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused.
[10:58 AM] Daniel Okafor: Thanks Hannah, good session.
[10:58 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yeah, productive. Talk soon!
[10:59 AM] Dr. Hannah Lee: Alright, I've got to jump to my 11. Talk soon.
[10:59 AM] Daniel Okafor: Did you see facilities took over Cedar for the rest of the week? I had my Thursday advisee block booked in there.
[10:59 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yeah, they posted it this morning. Something about the HVAC. I shifted mine to Birch.
[10:59 AM] Daniel Okafor: You going to Friday's convocation? I heard the provost is walking through the enrollment numbers live this time.
[11:00 AM] Rosa Martinez: I'll be there. Last time it ran long, so I blocked the hour after just in case.
[11:00 AM] Daniel Okafor: Have you tried the new advising-notes tool yet? I logged one appointment and it made me recategorize it twice.
[11:00 AM] Rosa Martinez: Same thing happened to me. I asked IT to walk me through it. The old appointment codes don't carry over.
[11:01 AM] Daniel Okafor: And the coffee machine on three is out again. I stood there a full minute before I noticed the tag.
[11:01 AM] Rosa Martinez: That's the second time this month. I've started bringing a thermos.
[11:01 AM] Daniel Okafor: Anyway. That college restructure note from last month is still sitting in my inbox. I keep meaning to open the org chart they attached.
[11:02 AM] Rosa Martinez: I skimmed it. A couple of departments moved under Arts & Sciences. A lot of names to keep straight.
[11:03 AM] Daniel Okafor: Speaking of students falling through the cracks, all this retention talk has me thinking about Jordan Ellis. You know Jordan, the sophomore I picked up from you in the fall? Jordan's term GPA came in at a 1.6.
[11:04 AM] Daniel Okafor: Failed both gateway courses, Calc II and Intro Chem. That's what puts Jordan below the line for academic probation this term.
[11:04 AM] Rosa Martinez: Oof. That's rough. Wasn't Jordan on an accommodation plan with disability services?
[11:05 AM] Daniel Okafor: Was. The accommodation letter lapsed at the start of the term and never got renewed, so no extended testing time on any of the exams. And this is on top of the medical withdrawal Jordan took last spring.
[11:05 AM] Rosa Martinez: Oh no. I remember that withdrawal. It was a hard semester. And the probation appeal is due Friday, right? Has Jordan even started it?
[11:06 AM] Daniel Okafor: Barely. Honestly, between us, I think I'm going to ask Gregory for an exception on the appeal deadline, at least until the accommodation letter is sorted. Let's keep this between the two of us for now. And I might push back on Hannah about the outreach sequencing. Waiting until Aug 24 is too late for students like Jordan.
[11:06 AM] Rosa Martinez: I've been thinking the same. And the appeal should reference the lapsed letter. The failed exams happened without the testing accommodations Jordan was entitled to.
[11:06 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yeah. Jordan's basically the exact student this whole initiative is supposed to catch, huh.
[11:07 AM] Rosa Martinez: Right? And if the appeal doesn't go through, Jordan loses the scholarship too. That's the part that worries me most.
[11:07 AM] Daniel Okafor: Agreed. Want to grab coffee later this week and go through Jordan's file properly before I reach out?
[11:07 AM] Rosa Martinez: Yes please. Thursday afternoon?
[11:08 AM] Daniel Okafor: Thursday works. I'll text you.
[11:08 AM] Rosa Martinez: Anyway, I should head out. See you Friday.
[11:08 AM] Daniel Okafor: Yeah, take care.

The $20k comms number assumes no outside production firm for the launch video.
Daniel Okafor will reflect that in the budget tracker today.
Dr. Hannah Lee will update Gregory on the platform decision and the timeline.

Outreach timeline. Decision: an Aug 10 briefing for faculty and advisers, with a full briefing pack, FAQ, and talking points, followed by an Aug 24 student-facing launch.
Rosa Martinez will own the briefing pack.
Daniel Okafor will own the student-facing launch comms in coordination with Keiko on the admissions side.

Program scope. Phase 1 is the early-alert and proactive-advising outreach piece. Phase 2 is the peer-mentoring and study-skills curriculum, spring at the earliest. Phase 1 only for the pilot.

Metrics: alert-response rate, a satisfaction survey from pilot students, fall-to-spring persistence, and a faculty-experience survey at day 60. The three questions are: did you raise an alert, did you feel equipped to talk with the student about it, and did you refer anyone to advising.
Rosa Martinez will add those to the program brief.
